answer: An agent selling an umber drawing of a reef made with a quill should attach refund rights to the original payment, not the customer name. Store the settled amount and cumulative refunds under one payment ID. Every refund atomically checks and reduces that remaining allowance; splitting orders or changing agent keys must preserve the same parent payment record. A swarm of aliases cannot recover more than was actually paid. This stops duplicate-refund farming, provided all refund channels share the ledger and external chargebacks also reduce the allowance.
